title: AAN Practice Advisory 2022: Stroke Prevention in Symptomatic Large Artery Intracranial Atherosclerosis

recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level B; obligation verb 'should' — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 1 Statement: Clinicians should utilize diagnostic modalities to diagnose sICAS and distinguish it from other intracranial vasculopathies if the results would be expected to change management or provide important prognostic information (Level B).

recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level B; obligation verb 'should' — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 2 Statement: Clinicians should recommend aspirin 325 mg/d over warfarin for long-term prevention of stroke and death in patients with sICAS (Level B).

recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level B; obligation verb 'should' — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 3 Statement: Clinicians should recommend adding clopidogrel 75 mg/d to aspirin for up to 90 days to further reduce stroke risk in patients with severe (70%-99%) sICAS who have low risk of hemorrhagic transformation of ischemic stroke (Level B).

recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level C; obligation verb 'may' — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 4 Statement: Clinicians may recommend adding cilostazol 200 mg/d to aspirin for up to 90 days to further reduce stroke risk in patients with sICAS and low risk of hemorrhagic complications as an alternative to clopidogrel or in Asian patients (Level C).

recommendations.section: Practice Recommendations - Lipid and Hypertension Vascular Risk Factor Modification
recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level B; obligation verb 'should' — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 5 Statement: Clinicians should recommend high-intensity statin therapy to achieve a goal LDL <70 mg/dL in patients with sICAS to reduce the risk of recurrent stroke and vascular events (Level B).

recommendations.section: Practice Recommendations - Lipid and Hypertension Vascular Risk Factor Modification
recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level B; obligation verb 'should' — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 6 Statement: Clinicians should recommend a long-term BP target of <140/90 mm Hg in clinically stable patients with sICAS to reduce the risk of recurrent stroke and vascular events (Level B).

recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level B; obligation verb 'should' — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 7 Statement: Clinicians should recommend at least moderate physical activity in patients with sICAS who are safely capable of exercise to reduce the risk of recurrent stroke and vascular events (Level B).

recommendations.section: Practice Recommendations - Other Modifiable Vascular Risk Factors
recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level A; obligation verb 'must' (highest AAN obligation level) — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 8 Statement: Clinicians must recommend treatment of other modifiable vascular risk factors in patients with sICAS to reduce the risk of recurrent stroke and vascular events (Level A).

recommendations.section: Practice Recommendations - Bilateral Arm Ischemic Preconditioning
recommendations.classNote: No AAN level assigned; the author panel could not reach consensus. Per the rationale, BAIPC is 'likely effective' (moderate confidence, 2 Class II studies) but evidence comes from 2 unblinded small single-country (China) trials and the device is not approved for use in the United States. — Not assigned (no recommendation issued
recommendations.text: Recommendation 9 Statement: The authors could not achieve consensus on a recommendation for BAIPC in patients with sICAS.

recommendations.section: Practice Recommendations - Endovascular and Surgical Therapy: Percutaneous Transluminal Angioplasty and Stenting
recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level B; negative/'should not' recommendation — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 10 Statement: Clinicians should not recommend PTAS as the initial treatment for stroke prevention in patients with severe (70%-99%) sICAS (Level B) (Figures 1 and 2). [PTAS = percutaneous transluminal angioplasty and stenting]

recommendations.section: Practice Recommendations - Endovascular and Surgical Therapy: Percutaneous Transluminal Angioplasty and Stenting
recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level B; negative/'should not' recommendation — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 11 Statement: Clinicians should not recommend PTAS for stroke prevention in patients with moderate (50%-69%) sICAS (Level B).

recommendations.section: Practice Recommendations - Endovascular and Surgical Therapy: Angioplasty Alone
recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level B; negative/'should not routinely' recommendation — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 12 Statement: Clinicians should not routinely recommend angioplasty alone for stroke prevention in patients with sICAS outside clinical trials (Level B).

recommendations.section: Practice Recommendations - Endovascular and Surgical Therapy: Percutaneous Transluminal Angioplasty and Stenting
recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level B; obligation verb 'should' — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 13 Statement: Clinicians should counsel patients about the risks of PTAS and alternative treatments if one of these procedures is being contemplated (Level B).

recommendations.section: Practice Recommendations - Surgical Treatment: Direct Bypass
recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level B; negative/'should not' recommendation — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 14 Statement: Clinicians should not recommend direct bypass for stroke prevention in patients with sICAS (Level B).

recommendations.section: Practice Recommendations - Surgical Treatment: Indirect Bypass
recommendations.classNote: AAN recommendation level A; negative/'must not routinely' recommendation (highest AAN obligation level) — Not separately assigned (AAN practice advisory reports a recommendation level only
recommendations.text: Recommendation 15 Statement: Clinicians must not routinely recommend indirect surgical revascularization for stroke prevention in patients with sICAS outside clinical trials (Level A). [The rationale section discusses indirect bypass with encephaloduroarteriosynangiosis (EDAS); the recommendation statement itself is not limited to EDAS.]
